frame: Rater frame: conservative home-layer test. If the assigned failure mode remains open, do not give 2. If evidence is a draft, optional extension, or marketing page, cap the cell at 1. Prefer the lower score when mixed.

C.promise: Scoped signed payment mandates resolve L4 moral hazard / commitment
C.evidence: Intent Mandate and Cart Mandate as W3C VCs with chain intent→cart→payment
C.failure: Revocation not consistently propagated into settlement per ledger L4 open issue
C.metric: Revocation propagation latency across rails; currently unspecified
C.locator: spec-ap2; ind-google-ap2-blog; ledger L4 entry T2

I.promise: Cross-layer binding propagates AP2 mandates to UCP and A2A-x402 rails
I.evidence: UCP spec binds payment to AP2; A2A x402 extension with Coinbase/MetaMask
I.failure: Binding is one-sided; revocation scope not enforced across seam

A.promise: Seven-property assurance coverage for agent payment mandates
A.evidence: Signed mandates, audit trail, price in cart; no dispute forum or rollback
A.failure: Execution correctness and recoverability remain unaddressed
A.metric: Count of addressed properties from seven; bin 2-4 → 1

EM.promise: Payment-agnostic rail supporting cards, stablecoins, RTGS for low-infrastructure markets
EM.evidence: Blog lists cards, stablecoins, real-time bank transfers as supported
EM.failure: Still depends on card/bank rails; no fallback without banking access
EM.metric: Institutional independence score; needs 2+ missing institutions replaced

S.promise: Versioned public spec with governance and multiple implementations
S.evidence: Public GitHub spec, reference implementations, 60+ named collaborators
S.failure: Single-vendor origin; limited independent adopters beyond collaborators
S.metric: Count of independent implementations; currently minimal

C.promise: Cryptographic payment evidence binds payer identity and amount to a service request.
C.evidence: HTTP 402 with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE; facilitator verifies and settles; base flow has no KYC.
C.failure: No atomic bind of delivery to finality; payment ≠ service fulfillment remains T3.
C.metric: Ratio of verified PAYMENT-SIGNATURE to successful settlement; delivery-guarantee gap.

I.promise: Links payment proof across Web2 (HTTP) and Web3 (blockchain) layers; integrates with ERC-8004 and AP2.
I.evidence: ERC-8004 abstract references proofOfPayment in off-chain feedback; AP2 blog describes x402 extension.
I.failure: Cross-layer binding is optional/advisory, not auditable end-to-end between L4 mandate and L5 settlement.
I.metric: Number of layers with auditable cross-boundary guarantees vs. total seam crossings.

A.promise: Four of seven assurance properties have observable artifacts; authorization and auditability strongest.
A.evidence: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (auth), optional signed receipts (audit), exact/upto schemes (exec partial).
A.failure: No recoverability (semi-trusted facilitator, no native dispute forum); no economic finality for service outcome.
A.metric: Property coverage count; dispute-resolution artifact presence/absence.

EM.promise: Usable without traditional banking, cards, or platform accounts; stablecoin and multi-chain support.
EM.evidence: 'Zero friction: No accounts or personal information needed'; EVM, Solana, Algorand SDKs; CAIP-2 IDs.
EM.failure: Facilitator is semi-trusted intermediary; stablecoins require issuer trust; no court-dependent recourse.
EM.metric: Dependency count on traditional institutions (banks, courts, card networks) vs. alternatives available.

S.promise: Public spec under Linux Foundation governance with multiple independent SDKs and IETF draft extensions.
S.evidence: x402.org spec; TS/Go/Python SDKs; middleware for Express, Next, Hono, FastAPI; IETF drafts for receipts.
S.failure: Marketing-driven adoption claims; compliance/receipt drafts are not yet deployed artifacts.
S.metric: Versioned spec release count; independent implementer count beyond founding orgs.

C.promise: Order and refund state management across the post-purchase lifecycle
C.evidence: `spec-ucp` defines order objects with fulfillment events and refund adjustment types
C.failure: Post-purchase state and refund portability remain merchant-specific (L6 ledger T4)
C.metric: Cross-merchant portability rate of order/refund state

I.promise: Guarantees propagate across layer seams via REST/MCP/A2A transports and AP2/VC bindings
I.evidence: `spec-ucp` documents transits over REST, MCP, A2A; built-in AP2 mandate support
I.failure: End-to-end propagation of guarantees across all connected layers not independently verifiable
I.metric: Independent protocol verify rate across seam bindings

A.promise: Partial assurance across execution tracking, authorization linkage, and audit traces
A.evidence: OAuth 2.0 identity linking; order/fulfillment objects; refund adjustments; webhook records
A.failure: No enforceable mandate-scope check; no end-to-end auditable reconstruction; no dispute protocol
A.metric: Property coverage count across seven assurance dimensions

EM.promise: Hybrid MoR design with web fallback should reduce some dependency on formal rails
EM.evidence: `ind-agenticplug-tracker` notes hybrid model; `continue_url` degrades to web checkout
EM.failure: Payment finality still requires PSP/card/bank rails; OAuth identity link needs platform trust
EM.metric: Usability rate in environments without banking or platform support

S.promise: Versioned public specification with named governance and vendor adoption
S.failure: Consortium-driven rather than independent standards-body process; limited independent implementer count
S.metric: Number of independent implementations against published spec

C.promise: On-chain identity + reputation registry to mitigate adverse selection.
C.evidence: Three registries (identity, reputation, validation) with `supportedTrust` flag.
C.failure: T1: identity ≠ capability; 'cannot cryptographically guarantee advertised capabilities are functional'.
C.metric: Sybil-inflation rate and percentage of capability claims with cryptographic verification.
C.locator: spec-erc8004, Security Considerations; L1 ledger consensus

I.promise: Optional adapters to A2A/MCP/ENS/DID and x402 may link upward.
I.evidence: Endpoint fields and `x402Support` flag in spec; feedback MAY include `proofOfPayment`.
I.failure: No auditable binding to AP2 mandates or x402 settlement; cross-chain consistency unspecified.
I.metric: Number of protocols that can verify an ERC-8004 registration natively.

A.promise: Reputation tracking and validation hooks for assurance.
A.evidence: On-chain feedback records, `getSummary` with client filter; validation hooks for TEE/zkML.
A.failure: Economic finality, pricing correctness, and recoverability absent; execution scope unbound.
A.metric: Count of traceable transactions from registry event to observable outcome.

EM.promise: Chain-native identity and reputation usable without courts/cards.
EM.evidence: Self-custodial, on-chain registries; optional x402 for payment-agnostic operation.
EM.failure: Still requires wallet, RPC access, and blockchain fees as fallback.
EM.metric: Operations completable with only a mnemonic seed and public RPC.

S.promise: Stable, governed spec with multiple implementers.
S.evidence: Public EIP draft with institutional signatories (MetaMask, EF, Google, Coinbase).
S.failure: Draft status; no versioned finalized spec; limited independent implementations.
S.metric: Number of independent reference implementations and governance decisions recorded.

C.promise: Capability discovery binds advertised tools to client requests.
C.failure: No binding of advertised capability to demonstrated performance (L2) and multi-hop intent fidelity unbound (L3, T2).
C.metric: Rate of tool-call log matching principal intent per invocation.
C.locator: protocol-root-model-context-protocol; sur-ehtesham2025-agent-interop; spec layer ledger L2/L3

I.promise: Open transport binding AI apps to tools and data sources across vendor boundaries.
I.evidence: Clients: Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor; first-class transport per UCP; multi-implementer ecosystem.
I.failure: No agent-to-agent payment, mandate, or dispute binding (A2A 'What A2A is not'); governance gaps noted in measurement paper.
I.metric: Number of independent clients and tool servers using shared schema.

A.promise: Partial assurance via capability discovery and tool-call traceability.
A.evidence: Capability registry; user-mediated delegated access; tool-call logs; broad implementer base.
A.failure: No economic finality, pricing correctness, compliance continuity, or recoverability artifacts in spec.
A.metric: Proportion of seven properties with observable artifact; exec-fidelity audit coverage.

EM.promise: Reduced dependence on traditional intermediaries via direct agent-to-tool contracts.
EM.evidence: Client-server model works without banks/cards; user-mediated access; no KYC dependency in core spec.
EM.failure: Still requires platform/tool-server availability and internet access; no fallback for absent infrastructure.
EM.metric: Operational count in low-banking-density environments; tool-server availability rate.

S.promise: Stable, governed, widely adopted open standard.
S.evidence: Versioned docs (2026-07-28); multiple independent client/server implementations; public intro and spec pages.
S.failure: No named governance body or standards-process record in packet; survey notes governance gaps.
S.metric: Count of independent implementations; versioned spec release cadence.

C.promise: Advertise agent capability via Agent Card; route tasks to matching agents
C.evidence: Agent Card JSON with capabilities/skills/endpoint; task lifecycle with ID
C.failure: L3 failure T2—multi-hop handoff unbound; completion trace ≠ intent fidelity
C.metric: Bind advertised capability to demonstrated outcome per task

I.evidence: Explicitly complementary to MCP; AP2 described as extension for payments; UCP transport via Agent Card URL
I.failure: Optional binding only; no auditable cross-layer mandate propagation

EM.promise: Operate over standard HTTP/S without proprietary rails

EM.failure: Still requires platform infrastructure, TLS, stable network; no offline or lightweight-path artifact

S.promise: Versioned spec under Linux Foundation governance; multi-SDK availability

C.failure: L7/T5 open: interface transparency does not create enforceable remedy; no mandate/dispute objects

I.evidence: Docs position AG-UI next to MCP (tools) and A2A (agents); no cross-layer binding specification
I.failure: No auditable binding to L4/L5/L8 guarantees; propagation across layer seams is unspecified

EM.failure: Depends on existing UI/tech stack; no reduction in institutional dependence

S.promise: Open protocol with SDKs and framework integrations
S.evidence: GitHub repo and integration table on docs site; no versioned spec, no named governance body
S.failure: No standards-body process; no independent implementation census beyond listed SDKs

C.promise: Contract enforcement via crowdsourced jury dispute resolution
C.evidence: Court product with staked jurors, appeals hierarchy, ERC-792 arbitration standard, live since 2019
C.failure: No native agent-speed standard; enforcement latency is days-scale, not machine transaction speed
C.metric: Mean resolution time from Court logs; proportion of disputes resolved below agent-latency threshold

I.promise: No specified binding to L4/L5/L6 protocols
I.evidence: Kleros operates as standalone L8 forum; no protocol-level integration clause with AP2, x402, or UCP
I.failure: Not wired as default remedy into lower-layer specs; cross-jurisdiction enforcement not automatic
I.metric: Number of upper-layer protocol specs referencing Kleros as a required or verifiable enforcement rail

A.promise: Some dispute-assurance properties via on-chain arbitration

A.failure: Recovery exists but is human-scale (days); no automated compliance, pricing, or end-to-end auditability

EM.promise: Reduced dependence on traditional courts and banks
EM.evidence: On-chain dispute resolution; does not require card networks or KYC bureaus; Proof of Humanity for identity
EM.failure: Still requires cryptocurrency access, internet connectivity, and crypto-custody knowledge absent in many EM contexts
EM.metric: Count of required traditional institutions eliminated vs. new crypto-infrastructure dependencies introduced

S.promise: Public specification with governance and deployed products
S.evidence: White paper (Lesaege et al.), ERC-792/ERC-1497 standards, cooperative governance via Snapshot, live products (Court, Escrow, Curate)
S.failure: Governance structure is cooperative but not a formal standards-body process; independent implementer count unverifiable from packet alone
